author: Ranjith Shivahari
title: Offer or Just
hook: price tag is not a promise!
simple_words: An offer can be accepted to make a contract. An invitation only asks people to come and make an offer.

definitions.meaning: A person shows willingness to do or not do something, to get the other's assent, and is ready to be bound once assent is given.
definitions.note: Willingness to be bound is the test

definitions.meaning: A step before an offer. It only invites others to make offers, so it cannot be accepted to form a contract.
definitions.note: Not an offer, no acceptance possible

key_points: Test: did the maker intend to be ==bound== on simple acceptance?
Goods with price tags, price lists, catalogues, tender notices and auction announcements are invitations to offer.
A reward advertisement for anyone who performs a condition is a ==general offer== (Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.).
!!Do not decide by the word used. Decide by intention to be bound.!!

rows: Ready to be bound on acceptance
Only invites others to make offers
Reward ad; a bid at auction

insight.text: For displayed goods, the customer makes the offer and the seller accepts or refuses it.

memory_trick.explanation: You carry the tagged item to the counter. That act is your offer. The cashier accepts by billing it. The tag only invited you.

steps: Ask: ready to be bound on yes?
If yes, it is an offer
If it only invites bids, it is an invitation
Check for a general offer (reward ad)
exam_tip: In MCQs, look for words like price list, catalogue, tender notice, auction announcement. These point to invitation to offer.

doubt.question: Why is a price tag not an offer?
doubt.answer: If it were, the shopkeeper would be bound to sell to every taker, even for a wrong tag or no stock. So the customer offers and the seller may accept or refuse.

mistakes.wrong: Goods with a price tag in a shop window are an offer.
mistakes.right: They are an invitation to offer. The customer's offer to buy is accepted by the seller.

mistakes.wrong: A tender notice is an offer and each tender is an acceptance.
mistakes.right: The notice is an invitation. Each tender is an offer, and the notice issuer accepts one.

mistakes.wrong: A reward advertisement is only an invitation to offer.
mistakes.right: It is a general offer. Performing the condition is acceptance (Carlill v. Carbolic Smoke Ball Co.).

mistakes.wrong: At an auction, the bid is an acceptance.
mistakes.right: The auction announcement is an invitation. The bid is an offer, accepted by the auctioneer.

reviewer_note: Definition paraphrases s.2(a). No section numbers are quoted in the slides. Please confirm that the auction bid and the tender submission wording matches the ICAI study material.
check_notes: Writer: Definition paraphrases s.2(a). No section numbers are quoted in the slides. Please confirm that the auction bid and the tender submission wording matches the ICAI study material.

Checker 1: Step 4 ('If it only invites bids, it is an invitation'): the wording is too narrow. Bids only fit auctions and tenders, but price tags and catalogues invite offers to buy, not bids. Better: 'If it only invites others to make offers (bids, tenders, offers to buy), it is an invitation to offer.'

Checker 1: Steps 2–5 order: a reward ad is already treated as an offer at Steps 2–3, so checking for a general offer last reads as an afterthought. Better: put the general-offer check right after Step 3, e.g. 'If yes, it is an offer. If it is addressed to the public at large, such as a reward ad, it is a general offer.'
